response.parser: n6(byte[]); consumer PlaudDeviceAgent.process_item_data(n6) forwards n6.d()/c()/b() to listener.bleStorage(total, free, duration)

emulator_deterministic.provenance: emulator-controlled values for the R1b virtual-link test (tests/test_r1b_get_storage.py). Structure is SDK-derived (n6 parser offsets); values are NOT hardware-observed. free/total presumed bytes (strongly inferred: both templates compute storageUsed = total - free); duration unit UNKNOWN (both templates ignore it).

response.minimum_structural_length_meaning: Unconditional parser prefix: 3-byte header + u64 free + u64 total. duration@19 needs length >= 27; shorter frames return early with fewer fields.
response.opcode_aliasing: No alias: n6 is the SOLE class with a()==6 among all 240 proto classes (bytecode scan). Callback routing via q.F still applies, but opcode 6 is unambiguous.
response.n6_evidence: CONFIRMED SDK-derived, 2026-09-21, from plaud-sdk.aar classes.jar bytecode (parsed with jawa, no decompiler): n6<init> executes b=u64@3, c=u64@11 unconditionally and d=u64@19 when length>=27. n6.toString gives real name StorageRsp and maps free<-b, total<-c, duration<-d. Consumer mapping verified through shuffled getters: n6.c()->b, n6.d()->c, n6.b()->d, so process_item_data pushes (total, free, duration) into bleStorage(total, free, duration), matching both templates' signatures.
response.transport_note: RESOLVED 2026-09-21 as ordinary ATT MTU expansion, no app segmentation: the Android SDK calls BluetoothGatt.requestMtu(255) on every STATE_CONNECTED (z.f, field default in z.<init>), stores/forwards the negotiated value in onMtuChanged, and consumes each notification as a single getValue() byte[] with no accumulation buffers in z/z$c. The 27-byte response therefore arrives as ONE notification iff negotiated MTU >= 30. Residual unknown: device-side MTU acceptance (firmware-side, invisible in app artifacts). The R1b virtual test's ATT MTU exchange is the source-backed equivalent. (The getPortVersion()<20 branch in onCharacteristicChanged is a legacy-device path, not a length gate.)
response.success_condition: n6 constructor succeeds and opcode equals 6
evidence: q.F callback chain constructs the response for opcode 6 and forwards n6 to process_item_data
PlaudDeviceAgent.process_item_data(n6) forwards to listener.bleStorage(total, free, duration)
iOS bleStorage(total, free, duration) sets storageTotal/total-free; Android bleStorage(total, free, duration) sets storageUsed/total identically
